blocks.text: Condo buildings in Zonings

The "zonings" page is the site's zoning directory ("Zoning Guide: Langley, Surrey, Abbotsford & Delta BC") — a card directory of municipal zoning bylaw summaries plus an address-check tool and an "ALR basics" section. There is no building list for this page by design: states that plainly, and carries the cross-city zoning frame that decides what condo product can exist where, with every contested item flagged rather than resolved by guessing. No market figures belong on this page and none are stated.
Streets, schools and getting around Zonings

items.t: The directory's territory is the site's Fraser Valley market area: Abbotsford, the Township of Langley, Surrey and Delta in full sections, plus a Mission rural-zone tail (RR7 / RR7s cards at the end of the directory).

The page's structure is the map: Abbotsford gets detailed agricultural cards (A1–A6) and rural cards (RR, CR, SR, SRH), then a collapsed "Residential and other zones (67)" set; the Township of Langley gets detailed rural cards (RU-1 to RU-14, SR-1 to SR-3B, CRE-1), then "Residential and other zones (25)"; Surrey gets detailed A-1, A-2, RA and R1 cards, then "(59)"; Delta gets detailed A1–A3 agriculture cards, then "(62)". Farm, rural and acreage zones get full cards in every municipality; urban residential and commercial zones get intent-line cards — the directory is built farm-first.

Where condo stock concentrates, in zoning terms: zoning decides the *form* attached housing can take in each city — apartment and townhouse zones (including Surrey's MR zones and the Township's RM-1 to RM-4 family in the collapsed sets) are where strata apartment product is permitted — but a zone card is never, by itself, evidence that any specific building exists or what its bylaws say.

The page carries a free property address-check tool (zoning, ALR status, lot size and other public map checks) covering Surrey, Langley City and Township, and Abbotsford addresses — notably not Delta or Mission addresses, even though both appear in the directory.

The page states it was "Checked against each official bylaw on October 2, 2026" and carries a "general information only… not legal advice" disclaimer. Zoning is per-parcel: which zone applies to a specific property, its ALR status and what can be built on it are checks with the municipality and the ALC, for any address, in every city on this page.

items.t: The bylaws behind the directory (name AND number, contested items flagged): Surrey — Zoning By-law, 1993, No. 12000; Township of Langley — Zoning Bylaw No. 2500. Two naming splits the page itself flags, recorded so the rebuild keeps the flags: the Township's RU-6 zone is named "Rural Processing Zone" in s.104.1 while its Section 200 heading reads "Agricultural Processing Zone," and RU-11 carries the same kind of split ("Rural Estate Winery Zone" / "Rural Winery Zone") — bylaw inconsistencies, flagged, never resolved by guessing.

Surrey frame (settled position): Zoning By-law No. 12000's residential zones R1 to R7 replaced the RF, RH and RQ zones on July 8, 2024 under provincial SSMUH legislation (RF-12/RF-12C → R4, shown on the page's R4 card as "Formerly RF-13, RF-12, RF-12C"; RF-SD → R6), and a secondary suite in Surrey is capped at 40% of the principal dwelling unit's habitable floor area — a "90 m² cap" is NOT current and appears nowhere as a suite rule in the Surrey cards read; the 90 m² figure on this page is the ALR additional-residence limit, a different rule.

Three suite regimes on one page, never to be mixed: Surrey's cap is 40% of the principal unit's habitable area; on ALR land a suite is permitted only inside the principal residence; and Abbotsford's A1 card states its own suite figure of up to 100 m² under that city's bylaw as the page summarizes it. Quoting one city's number for a property in another is the classic error this directory exists to prevent.

SSMUH, three different municipal implementations of one provincial law: Abbotsford carries dedicated SSMUH 1–4 zones; Surrey carries the full R1–R7 replacement set with former codes shown; the Township's SSMUH delivery sits inside its SR/R zone text (e.g., SR-1 and SR-3 cards describing small-scale multi-unit housing developments). For a condo buyer cross-shopping a house lot, this is the rule set that decides whether the lot can add units without rezoning.

ALR housing frame (applies on top of zoning in every city here): one principal residence without an ALC application at a maximum total floor area of 500 m² (no more than 1,000 m² of fill), a secondary suite only within that principal residence, and at most one additional residence of up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha; local governments can add further restrictions.

Township frame (as the page presents it): Abbotsford frame (as the page presents it): the A1 zone carries agriculture with one single detached dwelling, a secondary suite (to 100 m² per the card) and one accessory farm dwelling unit on lots of at least 0.4 ha, with an 8.0 ha minimum new lot; the A2 minimum rises to 16 ha.

Manufactured-home pad rents (where parks are discussed): pad tenancies sit under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, not in any zoning bylaw; the provincial pad-rent increase limit is 2.3% + proportional amount for 2026 and 2.2% + proportional amount for 2027. No pad-rent dollar figure is published here. RTB rent increases for ordinary tenancies are 2.3% (2026) / 2.2% (2027).

items.t: Surrey's 2024 zone replacement is the single biggest "old listing text is wrong" trap in the market area. R1–R7 replaced RF/RH/RQ on July 8, 2024 under provincial SSMUH legislation — any pre-2024 document, old MLS sheet or remembered zone code for a Surrey lot needs translating through the directory's former-code cards before it is relied on.

The Township is still adding zones. The directory's SR-3B card records that zone as added by Bylaw No. 6144 on July 27, 2026 — a live example of why the page carries a check date (October 2, 2026) and why a card is a summary, not the bylaw.

The directory itself flags two bylaw naming inconsistencies worth keeping in the rebuild: the Township's RU-6 zone is named "Rural Processing Zone" in s.104.1 while its Section 200 heading reads "Agricultural Processing Zone," and RU-11 carries the same kind of split ("Rural Estate Winery Zone" / "Rural Winery Zone"). If a search or a legal description uses the other name, it is the same zone.

Farm class is the zoning-adjacent question acreage buyers forget. BC Assessment's farm-class thresholds are $2,500 gross annual farm income for an operation of 0.8–4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha for a larger operation, and $10,000 for an operation under 0.8 ha, with applications due by October 31 — the directory's buyer checklist points farm buyers at exactly this check.

The page's address tool and its directory don't cover the same ground. The free address check covers Surrey, Langley (City and Township) and Abbotsford only — a Delta or Mission address can be read in the directory but not run through the tool, so those parcels go straight to the municipality.

A repeat fetch of the page returned a 429 from the fetch service, so the Delta section's tail and the Mission section's heading and opening cards were not re-read; the sections' existence is established (Delta A1–A3 and RS-series cards, Mission RR7/RR7s cards at the directory's end), but that segment's detail is not verified and should be re-read before the rebuild republishes it.

The page's title understates its own coverage. The title names Langley, Surrey, Abbotsford and Delta, but the directory also carries a Mission rural section — a buyer searching Mission zoning lands on a page whose title says it is not there.

items.t: The directory's territory is the site's Fraser Valley / Lower Mainland market area: full sections for Abbotsford, Township of Langley, Surrey and Delta, plus a Mission rural-zone tail (RR7/RR7s cards at the directory's end).

Structure as read: Abbotsford — detailed agricultural cards (A1–A6) and rural cards (RR, CR, SR, SRH), then a collapsed "Residential and other zones (67)" set (RS1 and SSMUH 1–4 through townhouse, apartment, commercial, industrial, institutional and N-series CD zones). Township of Langley — detailed rural cards (RU-1 to RU-14, RU-3A, SR-1 to SR-3B, CRE-1), then "Residential and other zones (25)" (R-1 series, R-CL compact-lot, R-2, MH-1, FH-1, RM-1 to RM-4, RU specials). Surrey — detailed A-1, A-2, RA, R1 cards, then "(59)" (R2–R7 SSMUH-era zones with former RF/RH/RQ codes shown, MR townhouse/apartment zones, commercial/industrial/business-park/CD). Delta — detailed A1–A3 agriculture cards, then "(62)" (RS/RD/RH/RT/RA series, core commercial, service, mixed-use Ladner, industrial). Mission rural tail. Then "ALR basics" and a six-item "Before you buy" checklist. Farm/rural zones get full cards in every municipality; urban zones get intent-line cards — the directory is built farm-first.

Where townhouse stock concentrates, in zoning terms only: apartment/townhouse zones (Surrey's MR zones, the Township's RM-1 to RM-4 family, Abbotsford's townhouse zones, Delta's RT series in the collapsed sets) are where strata townhouse product is permitted — permission is not existence.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Zonings

items.t: Form B (strata townhomes, region-wide): SPA s. 59 — monthly fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, CRF balance, insurance summary, with rules, budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and most recent depreciation report attached; within 7 days, max $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. This provincial layer sits on top of every zone in every city in the directory — zoning never substitutes for it.
Fee-simple contrast — plainly: a fee-simple townhouse carries NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees; municipal zoning (below, per city) plus any registered covenants/HOA govern instead.
Bylaw numbers per city — standing corrections carried in full (cite these, never superseded numbers)
Three suite regimes on one page, never mixed: Quoting one city's number for another city's property is the classic error this directory exists to prevent.

SSMUH, different municipal implementations of one provincial law: Abbotsford dedicated SSMUH 1–4 zones; Surrey the R1–R7 replacement set with former codes; the Township's delivery inside SR/R zone text (SR-1/SR-3 cards) under Bylaw 6020 with no 6-plex tier.

Farm class (BC Assessment, verified): thresholds $2,500 gross annual farm income for an operation of 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha for a larger operation; $10,000 for an operation under 0.8 ha; applications due October 31.

Taxes and rebates (buyer frame, region-wide): Exemptions: first-time buyers — first $500,000 at FMV $835,000 or less, partial to $860,000; newly built — full to $1,100,000, eliminated at $1,150,000. FTHB GST rebate — Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 (100% to $1M, phase to $1.5M, max $50,000, Mar 20, 2025–2031); New Housing Rebate 36%/$6,300/$350K–$450K; HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000/$8,000; CMHC 0.6%–4.5%.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Zonings
What trades here

items.t: What the directory does establish for land, at the topic level: the zone layer that decides a lot's form in each municipality — minimum lot sizes, permitted homes, and ALR notes on the farm/rural cards (purpose, main uses, extra homes, minimum lot, ALR note), with urban residential and commercial zones carried as intent-line cards. A zone card is never, by itself, evidence that any specific lot is for sale, subdividable, or serviced.

Fee-simple lots — the default form the directory's house and rural zones describe: a fee-simple lot carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees; zoning, ALR rules where they apply, and registered covenants govern instead.
Most subdivision of ALR land needs ALC approval, including parcels under 2 acres, as the page's ALR section states.

Farm, rural and acreage zones get full cards in every municipality; urban zones get intent-line cards — the directory is built farm-first.

A fee-simple lot carries none of this.

faq.q: Is there a "55+ zone" I should search in?
faq.a: No. No municipality in this directory zones for age. Age restriction is a strata bylaw under the Strata Property Act (only 55+ is valid), layered on top of whatever ordinary residential zone the building sits in — a "55+ search" is a bylaw-document search, not a zoning search.

faq.q: My Surrey listing says RF-12 — what zone is the lot actually in now?
faq.a: R4 Small Lot Residential Zone: Surrey's R1–R7 zones replaced the RF, RH and RQ zones on July 8, 2024, with RF-12 and RF-12C becoming R4 and RF-SD becoming R6; the directory's Surrey cards show the former code on each card so old listing text can be translated.

faq.q: How big can a secondary suite be?
faq.a: It depends which regime governs the property, and the three on this page must not be mixed: in Surrey the cap is 40% of the principal dwelling unit's habitable floor area (a "90 m² cap" is not current); on ALR land a suite is permitted only within the principal residence under the ALC frame; and Abbotsford's A1 card states a suite of up to 100 m² under that city's bylaw as the page summarizes it.

faq.q: Can I stratify an ALR acreage into condo units?
faq.a: No — strata plans in the ALR cause subdivision (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s.6), and most subdivision of ALR land needs ALC approval, including parcels under 2 acres.

faq.q: How big can a secondary suite be?
faq.a: It depends on the city and the land, and the regimes must not be mixed: Surrey 40% of habitable area; Langley City lesser of 100 m² and 40%; Township of Langley 120 m² cap; Abbotsford under 50% (A1 card states 100 m² as the page summarizes it); ALR — suite only inside the principal residence.

faq.q: Is there a "55+ zone" to search in?
faq.a: No. No municipality here zones for age; age restriction is a strata bylaw (only 55+ valid, SPA ss. 123.1/123.2) layered on an ordinary residential zone — a 55+ search is a bylaw-document search, not a zoning search.

faq.q: Can I rent out a strata townhouse long-term, whatever city it is in?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022 province-wide. STRs are separate: strata bylaw plus municipal regulation (and, in Pitt Meadows, an outright zoning prohibition).

faq.q: My Surrey listing says RF-12 — what zone is the lot in now?
faq.a: R4 Small Lot Residential: Surrey's R1–R7 zones replaced RF/RH/RQ on July 8, 2024 (RF-12/RF-12C → R4; RF-SD → R6), and the directory cards show the former code so old text can be translated.

A zoning directory and address-check resource: plain-English card summaries of the Abbotsford, Township of Langley, Surrey, Delta (and Mission rural) zoning bylaws with a link to the official bylaw for the zones, a free address lookup for zoning/ALR status/lot size covering Surrey, Langley and Abbotsford, an ALR basics section and a before-you-buy checklist — checked against each official bylaw on October 2, 2026 per the page, and general information only, not legal advice.

faq.q: What homes does the ALR allow on a farm parcel?
faq.a: One principal residence of up to 500 m² total floor area (no more than 1,000 m² of fill for its construction), a secondary suite only inside that principal residence, and one additional detached residence of up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less or up to 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha, without an ALC application — with municipal zoning still able to limit further.

faq.q: My Surrey listing says RF-12 — what zone is that now?
faq.a: R4 Small Lot Residential Zone: Surrey's R1–R7 zones replaced the RF, RH and RQ zones on July 8, 2024, with RF-12 and RF-12C becoming R4 and RF-SD becoming R6; the directory's Surrey cards show the former code on each card so old listing text can be translated.
